analysis.title: Three Strikes: Quants Suffer Worst Day Since August As Hedge Funds Notch Third "Never Since COVID" Day Of 2026
key_insights: Goldman Prime's Marco Laicini noted that from COVID through end-2025, all three broad hedge fund strategies never fell more than 80bps on the same day. In 2026 it has happened three times: 4-Feb, 28-Jul and 16-Oct (Thursday's session as described in the piece).

At 10:30am Goldman tracked Momentum down 3.4 SD, Crowded Longs down 1.8 SD and Crowded Shorts up 1.2 SD, which Laicini read as broader de-grossing, meaning funds cutting both sides of the book at once.
Goldman's HF VIP Long/Short pair (most popular hedge fund longs against most shorted names) was down 115bps on the day and down 10% since the drawdown began on Oct 8.

10:30am estimates: Global Fundamental L/S -0.9% (-1.2 SD), weekly drawdown -2.9%, YTD +9.6%. Asia-focused funds -2.6% (-2 SD), -6.8% MTD, +17% YTD. TMT-focused funds -2.0% (-1.4 SD), +11.1% YTD. Global Systematic L/S -0.9% (-2.6 SD). Multi-Strats -1.2% (-2.2 SD).

By the close Global Fundamental L/S had recovered to -0.5% (-0.8 SD), up 10% YTD. Global Systematic L/S fell 1.4% (-3.7 SD), the worst day since Aug 19, and is still up 20% YTD. Multi-Strats (equity book, 4.5x leverage) closed -1.2% (-2.2 SD).
Systematics were the only winners the prior day (+0.5%, 21.7% YTD) and gave it all back as momentum flipped. Systematic funds are short the losers, and the losers became the winners.

Goldman's Peter Callahan said the current episode differs from the July unwind, which felt mostly technical. This one raises debate over which 'wall of worry' is most acute into year end: earnings, elections, rates/credit, ROIC, inflation.
The 30Y yield fell 11bps on the day and Treasuries rallied as the bond market priced the deflationary side of an AI bust. The author says nobody is worried about the basis trade yet.

Goldman's Himanshu Deshmukh: Asia Fundamental L/S managers lost 2.6% Thursday, -6.8% MTD, YTD down to 16.7% ('back to July lows'), about 23 points below the ~40% end-of-June peak. The October drawdown is attributed mainly to beta and asset-selection alpha, followed by Volatility, Info Tech and Korea tilts.

Asian equities were net sold on the Prime book (-1.0 SD), led by Korea and Taiwan, with long sales exceeding short covers 3 to 1. Korea and Taiwan selling was dominated by long unwinds in AI. Cumulative 2026 net selling in Korea is around 13% of Asia net MV.
The Kospi is in a bear market, down exactly 20% from its high.

Korea net allocations fell 75bps MTD to 3.64% (32nd percentile one-year, 86th percentile five-year). Gross allocation is 2.59% (41st percentile one-year, 88th percentile five-year). The chart runs through Oct 13.

Taiwan has been barely touched: gross allocation is near all-time highs (94th percentile one-year, 99th percentile five-year). Foreign investors pulled a record ~$9.3B out of Taiwan in a single session this week.
Asia Info Tech is about 9% of global gross and around 18% of global net exposure in the Prime book, roughly three times its share of net at the start of 2025.

Goldman's London sales team: credit is forcing a rethink of how quickly the AI capex cycle can be financed and delivered, with the positioning unwind amplifying the move. With AI exposure materially reduced, discretionary nets low and rates rallying, trading sees pockets of overreaction, though financing constraints remain real.

Rich Privorotsky: 'a lot of bad news is now getting priced', neoclouds are down 20% in five sessions while quality has rallied in 16 of 18 sessions with an RSI of 83. His view: 'My gut is we've overreacted in pockets.'

Goldman's sentiment indicator has been negative six straight weeks, latest reading -1.3. The AI trade is 'still long, but now a 6 out 10 in terms of length and much cleaner than it was in Jun/July.' The desk net sold $10.5B of TMT in the past six sessions. Callahan: NDX forward P/E is back to ~21x, the lows since the AI cycle began in 2023.

The author disagrees with the desks. Net exposure to AI names is still in the 83rd percentile on a three-year view and Prime book gross leverage is in the 94th percentile of five years. Gross is 310% and diverging from net to an unprecedented degree, so the de-gross is not finished.

The author argues that Friday's OpEx removes some of the positive-gamma cushion that has kept the S&P calm (the index bounced off its 50DMA), so the next leg of the unwind may show up in the index. Falling yields from an AI bust could give the Fed an excuse to stop hiking.

sector_views.rationale: The author expects further de-grossing in crowded AI and momentum positions, citing 310% Prime gross, 94th percentile gross leverage and 83rd percentile net exposure. Goldman's trading desks see pockets of overreaction and a bounce.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Treasuries rallied as the bond market priced the deflationary side of an AI bust. The author says falling yields could give the Fed a reason to stop hiking.
Goldman's Callahan calls it the lowest since the AI cycle began in 2023, which is part of the case that the selloff has overreached.

risk_factors: Further de-grossing of crowded AI/momentum positions while gross leverage remains at the 94th percentile of five years.
Taiwan AI positioning near record size could be liquidated if sentiment does not improve. A record ~$9.3B of foreign outflows already hit Taiwan in one session this week.
Credit-driven financing constraints on the AI capex cycle.
Possible leakage of multi-strat de-grossing into basis trades.
OpEx removing the positive-gamma cushion under the S&P.
Year-end 'walls of worry' named by Goldman: earnings, elections, rates/credit, ROIC, inflation.

Goldman's chart of 2026 net flows by market shows Korea cumulative net selling around 13% of Asia net MV, while Japan, China and Taiwan hover near flat.
vol_and_positioning: Momentum -3.4 SD, Crowded Longs -1.8 SD and Crowded Shorts +1.2 SD at 10:30am: Goldman reads this as broad de-grossing, with crowded factors paying for it.
Global Systematic L/S -1.4% (-3.7 SD) at the close, the worst day since Aug 19 and the only worse print in the past year per Goldman's z-score chart. Systematic YTD +20%.
HF VIP Long/Short pair -115bps on the day and -10% since Oct 8.
Prime book gross at 310% and diverging from net to an unprecedented degree. AI net exposure is in the 83rd percentile (3-year) and gross leverage in the 94th percentile (5-year).
Hedge funds round-tripped all net AI buying since January 2025 in five sessions and sold AI stocks at the second-fastest pace in a year (flows through Wednesday).

Korea net allocation 3.64% (32nd percentile 1-year, 86th percentile 5-year), gross 2.59% (41st percentile 1-year, 88th percentile 5-year). Taiwan gross allocation is in the 94th percentile 1-year and 99th percentile 5-year.
Asia Info Tech is about 9% of global gross and about 18% of global net in the Prime book.
Goldman sentiment indicator at -1.3, negative six straight weeks. AI trade length is 6 out of 10. The desk net sold $10.5B of TMT over six sessions.
Friday OpEx reduces the positive-gamma cushion that has supported the S&P. The index bounced off its 50DMA.
cross_bank_references: The author (ZeroHedge) disagrees with Goldman's trading desks on pockets of overreaction: 'we would take the under'.
Callahan notes the current episode differs from the July momentum unwind, which he called mostly technical.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's desks see pockets of overreaction. AI exposure is materially reduced, discretionary nets are low, rates are rallying, sentiment is at -1.3, AI trade length is 6/10 and NDX forward P/E is ~21x, the lowest since 2023.
tension_points.bear_case: The author says the de-gross is unfinished: Prime gross is 310%, gross leverage is in the 94th percentile of five years, AI net exposure is in the 83rd percentile of three years, and Taiwan allocations are at five-year highs. Friday's OpEx removes positive-gamma support under the S&P.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Prime book gross exposure coming down materially from 310% would end the broad de-gross. A drop in the S&P through its 50DMA after OpEx would confirm the bear case.
